observation.visible_scene: A low-angle shot on an outdoor basketball court (green perimeter fence, trees, apartment buildings, a hoop and a parked car in the background) shows a player in red shorts, a black top, black knee sleeves and black-and-white sneakers, with tattoos on the arms and legs. The player is dribbling a dark/black basketball; the clip is a mid-action crop, so the dribbling is already in progress at the first frame and still ongoing at the last.
visible_changes: The basketball appears with strong motion blur, indicating rapid vertical/horizontal movement; in the first frames it is at the right side of the image near the player's hand, then drops out of view (frames ~3-13) while the player's hand continues an up-and-down dribbling motion.

From about frame 14 the ball re-enters at the right edge and travels across the frame toward the center and then to the left (frames ~16-33), with the player's reaching arm/hand tracking it, consistent with a side-to-side / between-the-legs dribble pattern.
After the leftward pass, the ball moves back toward the center-right of the frame (frames ~34-41) as the hand continues to dribble; the player's stance stays wide with legs apart throughout.

The background elements (parked car at left, hoop position, fence) shift progressively toward the left edge and partly out of frame, indicating camera panning/tracking or lateral movement of the subject relative to the scene, rather than the ball alone moving.
The player's body, shorts, knee sleeves, shoes and tattoos remain persistent and unchanged in appearance across the segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the dribbling sequence began before the crop and whether it continues into a move, shot, or turnover after the last frame.
The exact identity of the ball's brand/markings, which are blurred by motion.
uncertain_details: Whether the background shift is camera panning or the player moving laterally; the low-angle framing makes this hard to disambiguate.
The precise dribble technique (crossover vs. between-the-legs vs. in-place) at each moment, since the ball is motion-blurred and sometimes out of frame.
The number of ball contacts/bounces, which cannot be counted reliably from the sampled frames.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
